references.text: Describes Israel's victory over Og, king of Bashan, who is mentioned in Deuteronomy 3:11 as the last of the Rephaim.
Provides the context for the victory over Og, king of Bashan, whose enormous bed is described in verse 11.
Mentions Og, king of Bashan, as one of the Rephaim and confirms his belonging to this people of giants.
Refers to Og, king of Bashan, as the last of the Rephaim, the same description found in Deuteronomy 3:11.
Mentions the Rephaim as a people who lived in the region and provides historical background for this people of giants.
Mentions the Rephaim as one of the nations that lived in the land promised to Abraham.
Describes the sons of Anak as descendants of the giants (Nephilim), related to the Rephaim to whom Og belonged.
Tells of other giants among the Philistines, showing that there were several peoples of giants in the region.
Mentions Rabbah of the Ammonites, the same place where Og's iron bed was kept according to Deuteronomy 3:11.
